question.text: This president, the first one from the Democratic Party, sought to destroy the Second Bank of the United States by vetoing its recharter bill.
question.clue: This man signed the Force Bill to negate the Ordinance of Nullification, which South Carolina passed in response to his Tariff of Abominations.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the American republic.
swap.text: This rebellion, led by an eponymous Revolutionary War veteran in Western Massachusetts, highlighted the weaknesses of the Articles of Confederation.
swap.clue: It ended with a defeat at Petersham, after which its leader fled to Vermont, as Governor James Bowdoin fielded an army led by Benjamin Lincoln and William Shepard.

question.leadin: The Election of 1824 was a mess.
question.text: The eventual winner, John Quincy Adams, was said to have entered a "corrupt bargain" with this man, who finished fourth in the election and became Secretary of State.
question.clue: Early on he worked under George Wythe and married Lucretia Hart, settling down on his estate of Ashland.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the 1824 Supreme Court case Gibbons v. Ogden.
swap.text: This Congressman from Massachusetts, a member of the "Great Triumvirate," represented Gibbons before the Supreme Court and successfully argued that interstate navigation rights were under Congress' control.
swap.clue: This man said an institution was a "small college" but that there are "those who love it" while defending his alma mater in Dartmouth College v. Woodward.

question.leadin: Vermont Congressman Matthew Lyon was convicted of violating one of these laws.
question.text: Name this set of Federalist-backed laws that stifled criticism of the government and made it more difficult for new immigrants to gain citizenship. They were created in an attempt to silence the Democratic-Republicans.
question.answerHtml: Alien and Sedition Acts [prompt on a partial answer]
question.clue: These laws required a 14-year pre-residency requirement before immigrants could become citizens.

swap.text: This tenth president of the United States was luckily several decks below when the explosion occurred. Whigs nicknamed this president "His Ascendency" after he succeeded William Henry Harrison.
swap.clue: That Secretary of State under this President negotiated a treaty that settled the border between Maine and Canada called the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.

question.text: This coauthor of the Federalist papers was embroiled in the Reynolds scandal, and use his influence to tilt the election of 1800 in favor of Jefferson over Aaron Burr after the failure of his proposed candidate, Charles Pinckney.
question.clue: This person was the most prolific of a group of three that published articles under the pseudonym Publius.

swap.leadin: Name these events in which the United States gained land.
swap.text: The United States gained the southern parts of Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico through this purchase.
swap.clue: Its namesake served under Andrew Jackson during the War of 1812 before becoming president of the South Carolina Railroad Company.

question.leadin: The final decline of this entity began when Roger Taney transferred Pennsylvania's holdings to a similar institution owned by Stephen Girard.
question.text: Identify this financial institution, very much disliked by Andrew Jackson, which was first chartered in 1816.
question.answerHtml: Second Bank of the United States (prompt on partial answer)
question.answer: Second Bank of the United States
question.clue: An opponent of this organization was the first cabinet appointee to be rejected by the Senate, after his recess appointment expired.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the controversial Orders in Council.
swap.text: James Madison once said that he would have delayed declaring this war with Great Britain if he had known that the Orders in Council had been rescinded. The Battle of New Orleans was fought after the peace treaty ending this war was signed.
swap.clue: Northern Federalists discussed succession at the Hartford Convention during this war.

question.text: This man, who was later killed at York in the War of 1812, was imprisoned in Santa Fe in 1806 during the same river exploration mission that discovered a certain mountain in the Front Range. His report on Santa Fe spurred American interest in the Texas territory.
question.clue: He died leading an expedition against modern day Toronto in the War of 1812.

swap.leadin: This man's son was killed by future Civil War general Daniel Sickles.
swap.text: Name this man who watched the bombardment of Fort McHenry and later combined his writing with a British folk tune.
swap.clue: This man prosecuted the would-be assassin of Andrew Jackson, Richard Lawrence, who was committed to an insane asylum for the rest of his life.

question.leadin: This agreement limited military capacity on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain to two vessels for each of the signing powers.
question.text: Name this agreement between the United States and Britain that was signed in the wake of the War of 1812.
question.clue: It limited the number and wright of naval vessels on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain. For 15 points name this 1817 agreement which provided twenty years of peace in border relations between the United States and Canada.

swap.leadin: Michael F. Conlin argued that antebellum sectional debates often drew on legal arguments in The Constitutional Origins of the American Civil War.
swap.text: In 1846, the National Anti-Slavery Standard singled out this clause as the Constitution's worst. This infamous "compromise" ignored Native Americans and counted the enslaved as fractional people to apportion representatives.
swap.answerHtml: three-fifths compromise [or three-fifths clause; or 3/5; accept Article One, Section 2, Clause 3]
swap.clue: One of its architects was a Pennsylvanian later nominated to the original Jay Court, James Wilson, while the other, Roger Sherman, had helped shaped a similar provision that allowed debate on this item to occur.

question.text: In December 1848, this president confirmed the discovery of gold in California. This former "dark horse" presided over the war that added California to the Union.
question.clue: During this man's administration, a dispute over Oregon made "Fifty-four forty or fight!" a rallying cry.

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. A co-conspirator of this plot named James Wilkinson received a ciphered letter that betrayed it, which he then delivered to the president.
swap.text: Name or describe this plot in which a politician was assisted by planters in an attempt to establish a country in Spanish Texas. This plot's leader was acquitted because he was found not to have committed an "act of war."
swap.answerHtml: Burr conspiracy [accept answers indicating Aaron Burr’s plot to overthrow the government or Burr’s plot to create an empire]
swap.clue: This plot was betrayed by the "Cipher Letter" sent from its leader to his co-conspirator, James Wilkinson.

question.leadin: This man referred to Jefersonians as "fre eating salamanders" and "poison-sucking toads," and he joined George Cabot and Timothy Pickering to form the Essex Junto afer he became furious at John Adams for nominating William Vans Murray as minister to France.
question.text: Name this Massachusetts-born Federalist, who wrote a bunch of essays for the New England Palladium.

swap.leadin: After the initial light artillery barrage against adobe brick structures proved ineffective, American soldiers at this battle adopted the Texan practice of "mouse holing" through homes and fighting hand-to-hand inside.
swap.text: Name this 1846 battle which ended with Pedro de Ampudia surrendering a large city in Nuevo Leon in Northern Mexico.
swap.clue: This 1846 battle in which, after capturing Federation Hill and Independence Hill, American soldiers engaged in house-to-house urban warfare to conquer a city in northeast Mexico.

question.leadin: John Randolph's claim to fame was founding this political faction. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this breakaway Republican group, formed in 1806 to protest Thomas Jefferson's straying from the principles of states' rights. They supported James Monroe over James Madison in the election of 1808, and their name reflects their status as an outside third party.
question.clue: John Randolph was a close ally of his cousin Thomas Jefferson before breaking to lead this political faction, also known as the "Old Republicans." This radically anti-Federalist faction opposed national land acquisitions.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the most ridiculous of scandals, the Petticoat Affair.
swap.text: The Petticoat Affair concerned this former wife of John Timberlake who married a U.S. senator a SCANDALOUSLY short time after her husband died.
swap.clue: Though once a supporter and friend of Andrew Jackson, their relation was severed when Calhoun joined his wife and other cabinet members in socially ostracizing this wife of the secretary of war for committing adultery.
